title: ClipCapture
description: Sidecar uploaded with every assessment clip (ADR-013). Lets the server analyse the clip against true vertical and real frame timing instead of the phone's edges and arrival time. Contains no identifiers beyond the pseudonymous session.

stepId.description: Step id from the assessment battery, e.g. "static.anterior".

view.description: Which side of the body faces the camera. left_lateral = the person's left side faces the camera.

width.description: Encoded frame width in pixels, after applying the clip's orientation.

frames.description: One entry per encoded frame, in order.

t.description: Seconds since the clip's first frame (presentation timestamp).

gravity.description: Unit gravity direction in the camera frame C of the oriented image: x = image right, y = image down, z = optical axis away from the camera. A level phone filming upright yields approximately [0, 1, 0].

intrinsics.description: Pinhole intrinsics in pixels for the oriented image, when the device reports them.

depth.description: Optional LiDAR depth track uploaded alongside the clip (ADR-020). Absent or null means the device captured no depth; it is never synthesised. The depth frames are a separate, sparser time series from the encoded video frames - they are NOT index-aligned with "frames" above, and each carries its own timestamp on the same clock.

width.description: Depth map width in pixels (256 on current iPad Pro hardware), after applying the clip's orientation. Lower than the video's width; see geometry/intrinsics.py for the rescaling convention.

encoding.description: Per-frame payload format. uint16_millimetres_deflate: row-major little-endian uint16 planar depth in millimetres along the optical axis (NOT range along the ray), 0 meaning no return, compressed per frame as RAW DEFLATE (RFC 1951) with no zlib header or Adler-32 trailer. Raw rather than zlib-wrapped because that is what Apple's Compression framework emits for COMPRESSION_ZLIB, and a name that implied a wrapper that is not there would send a reader looking for the wrong first two bytes. Enumerated rather than free text so an unknown encoding is rejected at the boundary instead of being read as millimetres.

scaleMillimetres.description: Millimetres per stored unit. 1 for the encoding above. Carried explicitly so a future fixed-point scale does not silently reinterpret existing files.

nominalFps.description: Intended depth capture rate, typically 15. Informational only; "frames" carries the authoritative timing.

frameCount.description: Number of depth frames in the file. Must equal the length of "frames"; the server rejects a mismatch rather than trusting either.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded depth file, so a truncated or swapped track is detected before any geometry is computed.

hasConfidence.description: True when each frame carries ARKit's confidenceMap (uint8 per pixel, 0-2) appended after the depth plane. Apple documents depth accuracy as highly dependent on this value, so a false here means the per-sample confidence gate cannot run and depth sampling falls back to its statistical gates alone.

frames.description: One entry per depth frame present, in order. A dropped depth frame is simply absent - gaps in t are expected and must not be interpolated.

index.description: Position of this frame in the depth file, from 0. Not a video frame index.

t.description: Seconds since the clip's FIRST VIDEO frame, on the same clock as frames[].t, so a depth frame can be paired with the nearest pose observation.
